sections.section_heading: Cold email is broken. Warm outreach is not.
sections.description:
Every B2B inbox now receives the same morning delivery: identical templates with a first name dropped in, a subject line built from a formula, and a "just circling back" three days later. Recipients recognise the pattern in under a second and delete on sight.

The problem was never email. It was volume pretending to be attention. Reply rates fell because the messages stopped being worth reading, and no amount of extra sending fixes that.

sections.section_heading: Written for one person, sent by real infrastructure
sections.description: Most tools give you good copy or good deliverability. The copy tools produce something worth reading that lands in spam. The deliverability tools land a template nobody answers. Both halves have to work.
paragraphs: What it does

Most tools give you good copy or good deliverability. The copy tools produce something worth reading that lands in spam. The deliverability tools land a template nobody answers. Both halves have to work.
Each email is composed for a single recipient, using their role, their company and a specific reason the message is relevant. No merge tags, no template skeleton.
Send across multiple connected mailboxes so volume never concentrates on one domain.
Builds and maintains sender reputation on every connected mailbox automatically, before and during a campaign.
Validates SPF, DKIM and DMARC on your sending domains, flags misconfigurations, and tells you how to fix them.
Filters invalid and risky addresses before a send, so bounce rates stay low and your reputation survives.
Positive replies move toward a booked meeting rather than sitting in a reporting dashboard.

sections.section_heading: If it reads like a template, it does not ship
sections.description:
The bar is simple: an email should read the way it would if you had written it yourself, on a Tuesday, to one person you had a reason to contact. That means no formulaic openers, no borrowed urgency, and no phrasing that exists because it performs well in aggregate.

Personalisation here means the reason the email is relevant, not the recipient's first name in a subject line.

content.text: A LITTLE MORE CLARITY
Good questions.
What is Outreach Engine?–

A B2B email outreach platform from Ladder7 NextStep Solutions. It writes each email for one recipient rather than filling a template, and runs the deliverability stack behind it: inbox rotation, automatic warmup, SPF, DKIM and DMARC validation, and address verification.
Is this a cold email tool?+

No. Cold email tools send one message to a list. Outreach Engine writes a separate email for each prospect, built on a specific reason the message is relevant to that person, which is what earns a reply rather than a spam report.
How is deliverability handled?+

Through four mechanisms working together: multiple connected mailboxes with rotation, an automatic warmup engine that builds sender reputation, validation of your SPF, DKIM and DMARC records, and verification of every address before a send.
Does it find leads for me?+
Not yet. Intelligent Lead Identification is in development and will surface right-fit prospects automatically. Today you bring the prospects and Outreach Engine writes and sends to them.
What is it measured on?+
Replies and booked calls. Emails sent is not a success metric.
Who built it?+
Ladder7 NextStep Solutions, which also builds Site 360 and L7 Nexus.
How do I get access?+
It is in limited beta. Request access and the team will be in touch.
